title: Adaptive KV retention decay and kernel-thresholding for fragment-density-aware prefill
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Frequent allocation/eviction churn in paged KV caches leads to increased decode tail latency and degraded GPU locality for mixed workload profiles. We see pathological cases where short-lived fragments displace long-lived ones and cause repetitive re-prefill work and kernel inefficiencies. Goal: introduce an adaptive retention-decay policy for KV fragments combined with a fragment-density classifier that drives an online kernel-thresholding decision. This lets the runtime retain fragments with high predicted reuse while switching kernels (dense vs sparse-optimized code paths) when active fragment density crosses a threshold, improving tail latency and reducing re-prefill work.
acceptance_criteria: p99 decode end-to-end latency reduced by >= 8% on mixed steady+burst workload under lab benchmark compared to baseline
KV page re-prefill frequency reduced by >= 15% for medium-tenancy simulations
Memory churn (evictions per minute) reduced by >= 12% without increasing average token latency
Feature gated behind 'adaptive-kv-retention' and 'fragment-kernel-threshold' flags with safe kill-switch
Canary rollout plan defined and dashboards created showing p50/p95/p99, eviction rate, kernel-switch count, and per-tenant QoS impact
design_notes: Retention-decay: compute per-fragment score = alpha*recency_score + beta*reuse_probability + gamma*stability_score, and map score to flexible TTL-like retention buckets rather than hard LRU evict immediately

Reuse probability estimator: lightweight exponential histogram of access intervals + tiny trainable logistic weight updated by online counters (incremental, per-shard). We prefer a shallow estimator over heavy ML models to keep overhead low.
Fragment-density classifier: approximate active fragment density per KV-shard using bloom-tier counters and subpage occupancy ratios. Output is a single float 0..1 representing density.

Kernel-thresholding: two kernel families exist in runtime: dense-optimized and sparse-optimized. When density < threshold_low, prefer sparse kernels; when density > threshold_high, prefer dense kernels; hysteresis introduced to avoid thrash.

Prefill scheduling: couple prefill priority with retention score so low-scoring fragments are admitted with low prefill priority; high-scoring fragments get expedited prefill slots during slack cycles.
Admission: introduce soft reserve credits per-tenant so critical latency tenants can opt into a higher retention bucket via tenant weight. Credits are bounded to avoid long-tail monopolization.
Telemetry: emit fragment score histogram, kernel-selection events, prefill queue latency, and eviction reasons for postmortem and live dashboards.
Overhead target: the estimator + classifier should consume <2% of GPU host CPU cycles and <1% extra memory per shard. Implementation must be lock-free on fast path or use shard-local coarse locks.
Fallback: when the classifier reports uncertain (low sample count), fallback to existing LRU-like policy to avoid worse outcomes. All decisions are reversible.
Tradeoffs: aggressive retention reduces re-prefill but can increase memory pressure under bursty tenant workloads. We mitigate via soft credits and eviction backpressure signals to autoscaler.
Security: no user data used in estimators; counters and histograms are aggregate only. Feature flagged to allow enterprise off by default for Private deployments.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype estimator and classifier in simulation harness (single-node microbench) to validate thresholds and hysteresis parameters
Phase 2: Implement retention-decay policy in KV manager with feature flag and unit tests; add telemetry spans and metrics
Phase 3: Integrate kernel-thresholding hook into kernel selector path and add safe early-exit validation for correctness
Phase 4: End-to-end bench in infra cluster with controlled tenancy mix; compare against baseline and tune alpha/beta/gamma
Phase 5: Internal canary on small percentage of hosted traffic behind rollout rules; monitor metrics and quality regressions
Phase 6: Gradual ramp to 25% then 50% then 100% if metrics stable; add customer opt-in for Dedicated/Private via config flag

metrics_to_monitor: KV eviction rate (evictions/min) and evictions per shard
Re-prefill count per fragment per hour
Kernel-switch events per minute and average dwell time in each kernel
GPU utilization and host-side CPU overhead of estimators
Memory residency distribution by retention bucket
Incidents or QoS regressions for high-priority tenants
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Mis-tuned thresholds may cause oscillation between kernels -> Mitigation: add hysteresis and minimum dwell time, simulate workloads before rollout
Risk: Retaining too many fragments harms other tenants -> Mitigation: tenant soft-credits and eviction backpressure integrated with autoscaler
Risk: Estimator overhead impacts host CPU -> Mitigation: keep estimator constant-time and shard-local; measure and optimize hot loops
Risk: Unexpected regressions in on-device kernels when switching -> Mitigation: safety checks for correctness, slow-path validation and rollback flag
dependencies: Observability: dashboard templates and alerting infra
SRE: canary host allocations for runtime experiments
qa_plan: Unit tests for estimator math and retention bucketing
Fuzz tests for eviction under bursty sequences
Microbench comparing kernel throughput and correctness under simulated densities
End-to-end integration in canary with synthetic tenants and trace validation
A/B run with traffic shadowing to validate no QA regressions
release_notes: Default off for Private deployments; enabled behind runtime-2.5 opt-in for Hosted
Known limitations: initial heuristic may need tuning for very small shard sizes
